main_text.p: aliquot diebus sequitur, quibus ad ortum Cosmi-cum adiectis Heliaci tempus colligetur.
main_text.head: Exemplum occasus Cosmici & ortus Heliaci.
main_text.p: Ante tibi eoæ Atlantides abscondantur, Cnosiaq; ardentis decedat stella coronæ Debita quàm sulcis committas semina &c. Poëta in priori uersu, omissa mentione temporis, certam occasus speciem annotauit, cum inquit At-lantides abscondantur Eoæ, id est, occidant matu-tine.

Loquitur ergo de occasu Cosmico, qui fit Sole è regione cum opposito signo prodeunte, At Ple-iades cum 4 Tauri ferè occiderunt Vergilij tem-pore. Sol ergo qui oppositi signi eundem gradum obtinuit nimirum 4 Scorpij. tempus, hoc est, 2 2 Octobris demonstrat in tabella ingressus Solis in 12 signa zodiaci.

Cumq; tempus notum sit, in altero uersu de or-tus specie quæritur, 22 Octobris Sol 4 Scorpij te-nuit, at corona borealis cum 27 virginis Romæ prodijt, Alexandriæ cum 7 eiusdem signi. Vterq; locus sequitur Solis locum. Intelligendus ergo ortus Heliacus, qui ante Solem in Scorpio uersantem ma-ne coronam prouehit & producit in conspectum, M 2 Estq;

page.notes: Marginal note at top right ("I" and a mark, handwritten or stamp) not transcribed. Text is in a mix of roman and italic; italic passages kept as printed. Possible misreadings: "Cnosiaq;" and "Vterq;" as printed; "Alexandriæ" printed as "Alexandriæ". Signature "M 2" is a gathering mark at the foot of the text, placed in the text block as printed.
